PullRequest.Title: agentHost: route early subagent permissions to the subagent chat
PullRequest.Body:
agentHost: route early subagent permissions to the subagent chat

A Copilot SDK subagent can send a permission request before the runtime bridges
the tool.execution_start event of that tool call to the parent session. The
host set parentToolCallId only from the tracked tool start. Thus the approval
went to the parent chat, and the subagent chat showed the tool as running with
no approval prompt. The permission stayed pending until the user aborted.

- Record the agent ID from each permission.requested event that the handler
  must answer.
- If the tool start is not tracked yet, use this agent ID to find the
  parentToolCallId of the pending_confirmation signal.
- Remove the recorded agent ID when the request completes or when pending
  permissions are denied.
- Add tests for the session routing and for the side-effects behavior that
  keeps the approval pending in the subagent chat.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/346035

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSideEffects.test.ts`: passed (1941 tests). The new session test fails without the fix.
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: passed.
- Manual: with a temporary 3 s delay on bridged subagent shell tool starts (and their streamed deltas), the approval for a subagent shell command went to the parent chat before the fix, and the subagent chat showed the command as running with no prompt. With the fix, the approval appears on the tool row in the subagent chat.

Scenarios.Scenario: A subagent requests shell permission before its tool.execution_start event has been bridged to the host.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK permission callback performs its existing policy/sandbox checks, emits pending_confirmation, and waits for the user's decision. The added agent-ID association and parent lookup are synchronous Map operations and add no await or boundary to this critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The map scales with concurrently unresolved subagent permission requests, not session history or event volume; one entry is removed when each handler settles and all remaining entries are cleared on abort/disposal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Permission callbacks may overlap across distinct toolCallIds; each adds one independently keyed entry. There is no new fan-out or burst, and lookup/removal remain O(1) per request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing subagent agentId-to-toolCallId map supplies the parent association after subagent.started. The new request map is a transient correlation table rather than a reusable cache, with explicit per-request and bulk invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed set/get/delete/clear sites and the handler/event ordering are explicit, and the parent lookup is backed by Map.get.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The maximum number of simultaneous permission prompts varies by workload, but this affects only a pair of short strings per unresolved request and does not change the bounded lifecycle.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change adds bounded O(1) correlation work and no expensive boundary, scheduling delay, or retained session-history growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: A subagent write request builds a file-edit preview before displaying its permission confirmation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pre-existing handler checks file existence and writes the proposed content to the pending-edit-content provider before emitting the confirmation. The changed routing lookup runs only after those operations and does not duplicate or move them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether the target file exists for the preview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exists call per qualifying write permission request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existence check was already performed once per qualifying write permission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the preview-backed confirmation is emitted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write proposed contents to the pending-edit-content file provider and delete them after resolution/abort.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write and at most one cleanup delete per qualifying write permission request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same preview write and cleanup lifecycle existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write is on the confirmation critical path; cleanup is off the user-decision critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost remains linear in the number of actual concurrent write permission requests, with one pre-existing preview per request; the diff contributes only constant-time map operations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each qualifying write permission owns one pending preview and one routing-map entry keyed by toolCallId. The diff neither increases permission concurrency nor adds boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. Pending preview content and the new agent association are both removed on request completion and bulk-cleared during cancellation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the handler call flow places the unchanged preview operations before the added lookup, and no changed line invokes them more often.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File-provider latency depends on the target/provider, but its call count and critical-path placement are unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The existing filesystem work is neither introduced nor amplified, and the new correlation state is bounded to pending requests.

Scenarios.Scenario: The user aborts or disposes a session while subagent permission requests are pending.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Abort synchronously denies pending interactions; the new map is cleared in the same cleanup sweep. Disposal invokes the abort sweep before base disposal, so no new asynchronous cleanup blocks shutdown.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Clear cost is O(P) for P concurrently pending permissions, matching the number of retained entries and bounded by active unresolved requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single synchronous clear handles all outstanding associations; it does not perform per-entry I/O or schedule concurrent cleanup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both normal completion (delete by toolCallId) and abnormal termination (clear all) are covered; no negative entries or completed-request records remain cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the cleanup call path from _beginAbort to _cancelAllPendingInteractions to _denyPendingPermissions is explicit, and the changed clear is synchronous.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: P can vary with agent parallelism, but clearing an in-memory Map is small compared with the already-existing pending-permission denial sweep.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup-lifecycle or retained-memory regression; cancellation and disposal bound the new state.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and the complete diff. The production change adds a transient toolCallId-to-agentId correlation for early subagent permissions, performs only O(1) map operations on the permission path, and cleans entries on normal completion plus abort/disposal. Existing filesystem preview work is unchanged in count and placement. No actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
